title: Build a ProBuilder stage and research-lab background in the Test scene (reopened from raised-platform + screenshots)
description:
## Summary
Test-scene research-lab environment built with ProBuilder around the creature stage in `Assets/Test.unity`. Round 1 added a raised circular stage plus multi-angle screenshots. Round 2 rebuilt the stage in ProBuilder with a full lab background, then made the ceiling light functional with emissive shader materials and added CRT consoles, test tubes and science equipment. Round 3 (2026-09-13) adds specimen vats and table beakers, repairs misplaced props and light alignment, and adds model detail.

## User Mandate
> "Use your unity mcp access to test out the mcp usage and try to do things within the scene and navigate around according to what you have learned. You should be able to take screenshots of the creature from multiple angles and maybe add a raised circular/cylinder platform (keep the top at Y=0 and move the floor down a bit) That should be a little stage for the creature. Do this in the test scene"

STRICT. Binding constraints:
- Work in the test scene (`Assets/Test.unity`).
- Platform is circular/cylindrical with its top at exactly Y=0; the floor sits below the platform top.
- Screenshots of the creature from multiple angles are part of the deliverable.

> "Review this task given to another agent and completed, though it is being reopened for further work. I want you to use probuilder to make a proper stage. Make the center stage larger and create a research lab background using probuilder tools"

STRICT (round 2). Binding constraints:
- The stage is built with ProBuilder meshes, not plain Unity primitives.
- The center stage is larger than the previous radius-4.5 platform.
- A research-lab background is created with ProBuilder tools.
- Round 1 constraints still hold.

> "We should make the ceiling light functional (as much as possible), or at least use a really emissive texture. I also want testubes and computer monitors in the background. Especially if they can be large retro console computers with crt monitors and science equipement"

> "Shader/material, not texture"

STRICT (round 2b). Binding constraints:
- The ceiling light is functional as far as possible (real Light components) plus an emissive material.
- The emissive look uses a shader/material, NOT an emissive texture image.
- Add test tubes, computer monitors (large retro CRT console computers), and science equipment.

> "I would like a few of these vats as well. And if we can make beakers for the table too, that would be great. Lab Retro * B is stuck behind stuff"

> "The lab scope is floating and the centrifuge is leaning off the edge. The overhead lights should be aligned with the ring to make the sources more closely aligned with the ring light (they can be just a little lower). Add more detail to everything if possible and make the models more realistic"

STRICT (round 3, 2026-09-13). Binding constraints:
- Add several specimen vats modelled on the attached reference images.
- Add beakers on the table.
- Fix `Lab Retro * B` being stuck behind other objects.
- Fix the floating lab scope and the centrifuge leaning off the bench edge.
- Align the overhead lights with the ring circumference; they may sit only slightly lower.
- Add detail and make the models more realistic.

## Scope
- `Assets/Test.unity`: ProBuilder stage plus lab. Round 3 adds specimen vats, table beakers and a detail pass, and repairs prop placement.
- `Assets/Materials/`: `Stage*` and `Lab*` materials, including emissive CRT and fluid materials.
- No creature DNA, runtime code, or editor code changed.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Stage is a ProBuilder mesh with its top at Y=0 and radius greater than the previous 4.5.
- Research-lab background exists, built from ProBuilder meshes.
- Ceiling light functional (real lights) and emissive via material/shader, with no emissive texture.
- Test tubes, large retro CRT console computers, and science equipment exist.
- Several specimen vats exist, modelled on the references.
- Beakers exist on the table.
- No prop floats off the bench or intersects another prop unintentionally.
- Overhead lights are aligned with the ring, only slightly lower.
- Detail added; models read realistically.
- Multi-angle screenshots captured; console free of new C# errors.

## Validation
- World-bounds and intersection checks via `execute_code`.
- Screenshots under `Assets/Screenshots/`.
- Scene saved; static `ProBuilderMesh` count in `Assets/Test.unity`.
- `Scripts/Normalize-TaskRecords.ps1` and `Scripts/Test-TaskRecords.ps1`.

## Findings
- Round 3 diagnosis (`execute_code`): `Lab Scope Base` bounds x[-7.75,-7.05] vs `Lab Bench S` x[-6,6] -> the scope hangs entirely off the bench. `Lab Centrifuge` x[5.60,6.80] vs the bench edge at 6.0 -> 1.2 units of overhang. `Lab Retro Screen B` is intersected by `Lab Tank B` (x[-14.20,-11.80], z[-18.70,-16.30]) -> the tank physically overlaps the console.
- Round 2: a ceiling was required for "ceiling light" to be meaningful; a CRT emission gain of 4.0 blew out to white; `LabRetroCase` rendered near-white until darkened.
- `screenshot_multiview` auto-frames on full scene bounds; with walls at +/-22 the horizontal frames land outside the room. After a batch capture, `view_target` array resolution fails; `view_rotation` works.
- ProBuilder shape generation uses a centre pivot: a cylinder of height h at position y spans y-h/2..y+h/2.
- `git diff --check` flags Unity-generated `m_Data: ` YAML inside the scene; this is serializer output, not hand-authored content.

## Blockers
None.

## Next Step
Round 3: reposition the scope, centrifuge and tanks; align the ring lights; add vats, beakers and detail; then re-validate.

comments.body:
Implementation and validation evidence (2026-09-12, MCP for Unity 10.1.2)

Scene changes in `Assets/Test.unity` (scene saved):
- `Stage Platform`: Cylinder, position (0,-0.25,0), scale (9,0.25,9) → radius 4.5, thickness 0.5, top surface exactly Y=0. Verified world bounds min (-4.50,-0.50,-4.50), max (4.50,0.00,4.50).
- `Stage Floor`: Plane, position (0,-0.5,0), scale (10,1,10) → 100x100 at Y=-0.5.
- Replaced the primitive's degenerate `CapsuleCollider` (radius 4.5 vs height 0.5) with a convex `MeshCollider`.
- New materials `Assets/Materials/StagePlatform.mat` and `Assets/Materials/StageFloor.mat`, assigned to renderer slot 0.

Artifacts under `Assets/Screenshots/`:
- `screenshot-20260912-015757.png` — scene-view baseline.
- 6-angle contact sheets before and after the stage.
- `screenshot-20260912-020121.png` — positioned three-quarter view showing the raised platform lip above the floor with the creature's feet resting on the platform top.

Deviation from the mandate, surfaced rather than absorbed: the Test scene contained **no floor object**, so the floor was created below the platform instead of moved down. The visible "ground" was the scene-view grid and the default skybox ground band.

Skill corrections applied to `.github/skills/unity-mcp-operator/` after the live exercise proved the first draft wrong:
- `manage_tools(action="list_groups"|"activate"|"deactivate")` works here. The earlier claim that only client-side `activate_*` tools exist was incorrect. The reference file now carries the verified ten-group table and default states.
- Activating a group triggers a forced synchronous recompile and domain reload; the bridge drops for tens of seconds and reports `No Unity Editor instances found`, then `Unity is reloading; please retry`, then recovers.
- `execute_code` compiles with warnings as errors: `GetInstanceID()` failed with `'Object.GetInstanceID()' is obsolete: 'Use GetEntityId instead.'`.
- `screenshot_multiview` ignores `orbit_distance` and `orbit_elevations`; use `view_position`.
- `manage_scene(action="get_hierarchy", parent=<negative preview id>)` fails with `Could not connect to Unity`.

Console: no C# errors. The six `Command TCS timed out (N consecutive)` warnings are the bridge timeouts listed above, not scene problems.

Open item (out of scope, not fixed): the scene has two overlapping creature preview roots at the origin, which duplicate limbs in renders.

comments.body:
Round 2 implementation and validation evidence (2026-09-12, MCP for Unity server 10.2.0)

New requirement captured verbatim in the description under `## User Mandate` (STRICT): functional ceiling light or really emissive material, test tubes, computer monitors / large retro CRT console computers and science equipment, with the clarifying constraint "Shader/material, not texture".

Emissive via shader/material (no textures):
- `LabRingEmissive.mat`, `LabCrtGreen.mat`, `LabCrtAmber.mat`, `LabTubeLiquid.mat`: URP/Lit with the `_EMISSION` keyword enabled and an HDR `_EmissionColor` (ring 2.4x, CRT green/amber 1.8x, tube liquid 1.4x). Verified `keywordOn=True` and ring `emissionColor=RGBA(2.400, 2.304, 2.040, 2.400)`.
- No texture assets were created; the emissive look is material/shader only.

Functional ceiling light:
- `Lab Ring Light` (ProBuilder torus, radius 9) now uses `LabRingEmissive.mat`.
- 4 real point Lights parented under `Lab Ring Light` (`Lab Ceiling Light 1..4`) at radius 6.5, local y -0.35, range 46, intensity 8, warm colour (1, 0.94, 0.82), shadows Off (a point-light shadow is a cube map; four of them is not worth the cost here).
- `Lab Ceiling` added (ProBuilder cube 44 x 0.4 x 44 at y=11) so the ring reads as a ceiling light and the room is a real interior.
- `Lab Post FX`: global Volume with a Bloom effect (intensity 0.7, threshold 1.0, scatter 0.5). This is what makes the emissive materials actually glow.

New ProBuilder geometry (22 objects): `Lab Ceiling`; `Lab Bench S` (12 x 1.4 x 2.6 at (0, -0.5, -17.5)) + MeshCollider; `Lab Tube Rack S`; 6 test tubes alternating `LabTubeLiquid`/`LabGlass`; `Lab Beaker A/B`; retro CRT consoles `Lab Retro Desk/Monitor/Screen/Keyboard A` and `B` at x = +/-13.5 flanking the south-wall screen (Screen A green phosphor, Screen B amber; desks have MeshColliders); science equipment `Lab Scope Base`, `Lab Scope Arm` (microscope silhouette) and `Lab Centrifuge`.

Verification:
- `execute_code`: `Lab Ring Light` childLights=4; ring material `LabRingEmissive` `emissionKeyword=True`; Volume `Lab Post FX` found=True; every new object reports the intended material and Y range (bench S -1.20..0.20, monitor 0.30..2.30, CRT screen 0.60..2.10, keyboard 0.30..0.48, tubes 0.20..1.20).
- Scene saved; `isDirty=false`, `rootCount=45`.
- Static check: 41 `ProBuilderMesh` references in `Assets/Test.unity` (19 round 1 + 21 round 2 + ceiling).
- 12 `Lab*.mat` materials on disk.
- Console: 0 errors, 0 warnings.
- Screenshots: `tsk0243-round2-lab-final-front.png`, `tsk0243-round2-lab-final-quarter.png` (glowing ring plus ceiling light pools), `tsk0243-round2-retro-console_1.png` (green phosphor CRT), `tsk0243-round2-science-bench.png` (tube rack).

Findings:
- Without a ceiling the room read as open-air and the ring floated against the skybox; the ceiling was needed for "ceiling light" to be meaningful.
- A CRT emission gain of 4.0 blew the screen out to pure white and lost the phosphor colour; 1.8 keeps the colour while still reading as emissive.
- `LabRetroCase` at (0.72, 0.68, 0.58) rendered near-white under the new lights; darkened to (0.52, 0.48, 0.40).
- `git diff --check` now reports trailing whitespace on Unity-generated YAML lines (`m_Data: `) inside `Assets/Test.unity`. This is Unity's serializer writing empty ProBuilder mesh buffers, not hand-authored content; the scene file must not be hand-edited.

Residual risk / open items:
- 4 shadowless point lights + 1 directional light + Bloom now run in the test scene; cost was not profiled.
- The Bloom threshold is global, so the creature is affected by the same post-processing as the lab.

comments.body:
Round 3 implementation and validation evidence (2026-09-13, MCP for Unity server 10.2.0)

Requirement captured verbatim in the description under `## User Mandate` (STRICT): a few specimen vats, beakers on the table, fix `Lab Retro * B` stuck behind stuff, fix the floating scope and the centrifuge leaning off the edge, align the overhead lights with the ring (only slightly lower), and add detail / realism.

Placement repairs (diagnosed first with `execute_code`, then fixed):
- `Lab Scope Base` sat at x[-7.75,-7.05] while `Lab Bench S` spans x[-6,6] -> the whole microscope hung in the air. Rebuilt as a 5-part microscope (`Lab Scope Base`, `Column`, `Stage`, `Head`, `Barrel`) at x -5.7..-4.7, resting on the bench top at y=0.20. Verified `scopeOnBench=True`.
- `Lab Centrifuge` sat at x[5.60,6.80] with the bench edge at 6.0 -> 1.2 units of overhang. Moved to x=4.75 -> x[4.15,5.35]. Verified `centrifugeOnBench=True`.
- `Lab Retro Screen B` was physically intersected by `Lab Tank B` (x[-14.20,-11.80], z[-18.70,-16.30]). Both tanks moved to the west wall at x[-20.00,-17.60]. Verified `tankB_intersects_screenB=False`.
- Bench S rearranged so nothing overlaps: microscope x=-5.2, tube rack x=-1.6 with 6 tubes at x -2.85..-0.60, four beakers at x 1.2/1.9/2.6/3.3, centrifuge x=4.75.

Overhead lights:
- The 4 point lights were inside the ring at radius 6.5. They are now on the ring circumference at radius 9.0 and 0.6 below the tube centreline (world y=8.90 against ring y=9.50). Verified from the live scene: worlds (9,8.9,0), (0,8.9,9), (-9,8.9,0), (0,8.9,-9).

New content:
- 3 specimen vats (`Lab Vat A`/`B`/`C` at (15,7), (-14,7), (-8,-13)), 8 parts each: plinth, base, transparent glass body, metal collar, cap, hub, specimen sphere, and a feed pipe running to the ceiling. Each vat carries an inner fluid cylinder on a translucent emissive material, so the specimen reads through the fluid as it does in the reference images.
- 4 table beakers, 3 parts each (transparent glass body, emissive liquid, glass rim).
- Detail pass (24 objects): stage rim and a hazard floor ring, 2 ceiling cable trays, 3 wall panels, a wall conduit, 4 bench drawer fronts, CRT feet and boxes, and base/cap collars on all 4 pillars.

Materials:
- New: `LabVatFluidA`, `LabVatFluidB`, `LabVatMetal`, `LabVatGlass`, `LabHazard` (17 `Lab*.mat` total).
- `LabVatGlass` and the two vat fluids are configured as alpha-blended transparent URP/Lit materials: `_Surface=1`, `_Blend=0`, `_DstBlend=10`, `_ZWrite=0`, `_SURFACE_TYPE_TRANSPARENT` enabled, `RenderType` Transparent, queue 3000, ShadowCaster pass off. The fluids keep an HDR `_EmissionColor` (gain 1.6) at alpha 0.55.
- Note: `_SrcBlend` reads back as 1 (One) after the write, so the effective blend is `One / OneMinusSrcAlpha` rather than the inspector's usual `SrcAlpha / OneMinusSrcAlpha`. The visual result is correct, but the value differs from what the URP inspector would write.

Verification:
- `execute_code`: 111 renderers and **0 with a null material**. A null material renders magenta, which was visible in an intermediate screenshot before the assignments completed.
- `execute_code`: scopeOnBench=True, centrifugeOnBench=True, tankB_intersects_screenB=False, lights on radius 9 at y=8.90.
- Scene saved; `isDirty=false`, `rootCount=109`.
- Static check: 105 `ProBuilderMesh` references in `Assets/Test.unity`.
- Console: 0 errors, 0 warnings.
- Screenshots: `tsk0243-round3-lab-wide.png`, `tsk0243-round3-final-wide.png`, `tsk0243-round3-bench.png`, `tsk0243-round3-vat_1.png`.

Findings:
- The reported "stuck behind stuff" and floating/leaning props were real geometry faults, not camera artefacts: the scope was fully off the bench, the centrifuge overhung by more than half its radius, and the tank physically intersected the CRT console.
- ProBuilder shape creation assigns no material, so unassigned objects render magenta until `set_face_material` runs. A null-material scan is a cheap and decisive check after a bulk create.
- A camera yaw of 180 degrees flips the screen-space X axis, so +X world appears on the left. This inverted my first reading of the wide screenshots until I checked it.

Residual risk / open items:
- The scene now holds 105 ProBuilder objects, each with its own mesh and renderer. Draw-call and batching cost was not measured; `combine_meshes` is the available remedy if it becomes a problem.
- 4 shadowless point lights + 1 directional light + Bloom still run unprofiled, and Bloom remains global, so it also affects the creature.
- The vat and beaker glass is transparent, which adds sorting work and transparent-queue rendering.
